articles.title: Your Placeholder Text Is Lying to You: 4 Layout Bugs Lorem Ipsum Hides
articles.excerpt: Every mockup I reviewed this year used lorem ipsum. Several of those layouts broke in production - not because the design was bad, but because the placeholder text was too friendly. Here is what lorem…
articles.body: Every mockup I reviewed this year used lorem ipsum. Several of those layouts broke in production - not because the design was bad, but because the placeholder text was too friendly. Here is what lorem ipsum optimizes for, and what it quietly hides. 1. It has no long, unbreakable strings Lorem ipsum words are short, lowercase, and separated by spaces. Real content contains things the browser cannot hyphenate: a 90-character signed URL, an address like firstname.lastname@international-partners.example.com , an API token, a German compound noun. Those are what overflow a flex row - flex: 1 will not shrink below the content's min-content width unless you also set min-width: 0 (or overflow-wrap: anywhere ). You will never see that bug in a lorem ipsum mock.

articles.title: How to Use OpenAI WebSocket Mode API ?
articles.excerpt: TL;DR OpenAI offers two WebSocket API modes for different use cases: the Responses API WebSocket mode for agentic workflows with heavy tool calling (up to 40% faster for 20+ tool calls), and the Realt…
articles.body: TL;DR OpenAI offers two WebSocket API modes for different use cases: the Responses API WebSocket mode for agentic workflows with heavy tool calling (up to 40% faster for 20+ tool calls), and the Realtime API for low-latency voice and audio applications. Both use persistent WebSocket connections instead of stateless HTTP requests, reducing latency by eliminating repeated connection overhead and enabling event-driven, stateful interactions. Try Apidog today Introduction Every HTTP request to OpenAI's API pays a repeated tax: connection setup, authentication, and re-sent conversation state—even when you're continuing the same session. For applications making rapid-fire tool calls or streaming audio, that overhead is pure waste.

articles.body: CD Projekt Red has finally spoken up about the live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie . The company said it doesn’t want to do a 1:1 adaptation of the game, instead telling a new story within the same universe. "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish outlet PAP Biznes , via GamesRadar . "We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story." The Cyberpunk movie is being created in partnership with Parmount, now under the Skydance banner after the recent merger . The film will be produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura, of live-action Transformers fame.

articles.title: It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say
articles.excerpt: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system based on the Milky Way's gravity, including its dark matter.
articles.body: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier. That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University. The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun , they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15). A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today at 8:01 p.m. EDT (5:01 p.m. local time; 0001 GMT on Oct. 16), rising into clear blue skies above the Golden State's central coast. Such visibly striking launches are far from guaranteed; Vandenberg and its scenic surroundings are often blanketed by fog, making rocket watching in the area a dicey proposition. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-481 mission on Oct. 15, 2026.
